adjudications.why: 436 GB / 24.1 GB is about 18.1, while C = 17.5 requires the 24.9 GB whole-request basis. The quoted text uses both without reconciling the denominator.
The quoted clause is a scoped TCO assertion. The full mini-case assumptions, cost model, and quality terms are needed to test whether RAG + guardrails actually produces lower modeled TCO.

The parenthetical may be a self-referential labeling note. Need the surrounding section to determine whether 40 GB/s and 2.5 GB/s are actually presented as optimistic upper bounds or as measured/analytical values.

The quoted clause mentions a 2 s SLO breach, but the canonical TTFT budget/SLO value must be checked in the same section. If the canonical budget is 1.2 s, the finding is valid; if 2 s is the SLO, it may be a misread.

The quoted DP row mentions optimizer state and gradient all-reduce, which are training concepts. In an inference parallelism table, that is a domain-scope error unless the table explicitly includes training.

The table says KV -> ring, but the quoted text does not show whether the body actually establishes ring topology for context parallelism. Need the surrounding section to confirm whether ring is unsupported or merely abbreviated.
17.5 is derivable from 436 GB / 24.9 GB, but the finding likely concerns whether that value is properly established as canonical before use. Need the preceding derivation and all uses of 17.5.
The quoted cost string is truncated and mixes per-host, total, and per-1K units. A full cost ledger is required to verify whether $232.2K, $467.2K, $155,816.93, and $24.97/1K are on the same basis.
The finding concerns open-question wording. Need the full bullet to determine whether it presents a legitimate unresolved boundary or a claim that should have been resolved.
860 / 23.275 = 36.95, whose ceiling is 37, not 38. The printed ceiling is arithmetically wrong if the formula is as quoted.
1720 / 23.275 = 73.90, whose ceiling is 74, not 75. The printed ceiling is arithmetically wrong if the formula is as quoted.

The quoted clause distinguishes in-flight requests from registered users, but the full KV geometry and host count are needed to verify whether ~100 concurrent full-context requests is consistent with the canonical 17.5/host and 21-host values.

9200 + 3*865 = 11795 is arithmetically correct as total processed input tokens if the initial 9200 is processed once and then 865 tokens are appended per call. The issue is whether the wording 'only newly appended tokens are re-processed' makes the inclusion of 9200 misleading.
The quoted clause explains rho = 0.95 as a throughput derate, not a slot floor or failure reserve. Need the full chapter usage to verify whether other sections treat it differently.
The finding concerns whether fleet sizing must satisfy both KV-residency and throughput/latency bounds. Need the full bound equations and canonical numbers to test the logic.
The quoted burst calculation is internally correct: 200 rps * 1 s = 200 requests, drained at 50 rps in 4 s. The finding alleges two numerical errors, so the full worked example is required.
The quoted claim links sharding + caching to a p99 TTFT target across user growth. Need the full capstone assumptions, fleet size, and latency model to verify whether the claim is supported.
A canonical 70B model with 8 layers is not plausible; the intended value is almost certainly 80 layers. The caption as quoted contains a material typo.
The quoted clause is a definitional clarification about concurrent users. Need the full section to determine whether the book later uses 'concurrent users' inconsistently.
The quoted feasibility claim depends on the first-order model, SLOs, and host memory assumptions. Need the full paragraph to test whether 'analytically feasible' is overclaimed.

436 GB / 24.9 GB = 17.5, and flooring to 17 whole-context slots is arithmetically consistent. If the finding is that the chapter uses 17.5 and 17 without explaining the floor, the quoted text supports that issue.
40 rps over 730 h is about 105.12M requests/month, not 24.96M. 24.96M is closer to a 10 rps average over about 700 h. The volume basis is inconsistent as quoted.
The quoted cost range is arithmetically correct for 6 and 21 hosts at $20/hr over 730 h. The finding may concern a different inconsistency, so the full cost context is needed.
The finding concerns Figure 6.2 and whether the plotted quantity is request latency or TTFT. The rendered figure and full caption are required.
9200/300 is about 30.7, so the input/output ratio is correct. The finding likely concerns whether 'prefill-dominated' is overgeneralized; need the full mini-case reasoning.
9200 tokens * 2.62 MB/token = 24.1 GB initial KV, which is correct. The finding may concern per-request vs fleet-level interpretation; need the full sentence and context.
Same as the MiMo CH11-TTFT-SLO-01 entry: need the canonical TTFT budget/SLO value in the section to determine whether 1.2 s or 2 s is the correct reference.
436 GB / 24.9 GB = 17.5, and 9500 tokens * 2.62 MB/token = 24.89 GB. The arithmetic is consistent. Need the full finding to see what inconsistency is alleged.
The quoted host-count logic depends on whether 35 is the FP8-KV concurrency per host and whether the ~7-host prefill bound uses peak or sustained prefill. Need the full section.
The quoted ratios 0.33x, 1.63x, and 6.51x are consistent with a 56,500 tok/s peak prefill denominator. If Chapter 17 uses 19,800 tok/s sustained planning, the two bases must be explicitly reconciled.
$20.80 per 1M tokens is $0.0208 per 1K tokens. If the text says 'per 1K-token request', that is correct only for a 1K-token request. Need the canonical request length and intended unit.
This is the same Table 17-2 ceiling error as CH17-T172-01/02: 860/23.275 ceilings to 37, and 1720/23.275 ceilings to 74.
The finding concerns a continuity note declaring one section authoritative over earlier figures. Need both sections to verify whether the supersession is correct and whether stale values remain.
The finding concerns the drawn roofline intercept. Need the rendered figure, axis scale, and stated HBM bandwidth to verify whether the visual is inconsistent with 3.35 TB/s.
The finding concerns color semantics for post-training. Need the rendered figure, legend, and caption to verify whether blue/green encoding is inconsistent.

If 1% of requests are at about 5 s, the p99 marker cannot be 1.33 s unless the plotted distribution is not the same population or the 1% mass is not beyond the p99. As quoted, the figure is internally inconsistent.
The finding concerns the visual encoding of green backfill segments. Need the rendered figure to verify whether the legend and drawing are inconsistent.
The quoted placement of the canonical RAG workload on a ~21-server server tier depends on the canonical fleet size and tier definitions. Need the full section and related chapters.
Same cost-basis issue as CH12-ECO-01. Need the full mini-case ledger to verify host count, per-host rate, total cost, and per-1K unit.
The finding concerns PIES/CPS definitions and candidate pattern counts. Need the full definitions and table to verify whether 217 and the PIES subset are consistent.
10 rps average over 730 h is about 26.28M requests/month, not 6.24M. Using both as canonical values without reconciling the time basis is inconsistent.
The finding concerns whether open-question items are legitimate hypotheses or unresolved verification tasks. Need the full section to classify each item.
The finding concerns the caption's regime label and arithmetic intensity. Need the full caption and figure to verify whether '~0.2K FLOP/byte' and the regime description are consistent.
If the intended MoE 8-bit KV value is 0.0655 MB/token, printing 0.655 MB/token is a factor-of-10 error. The quoted caption supports the finding.
The finding concerns cost-ledger arithmetic across a table and prose. Need the full table, parenthetical base, and prose values to verify closure.
The finding concerns per-request on-node transfer time versus the figure's GPU grid and per-GPU rate. Need the rendered figure and full labels to verify the arithmetic.
The finding concerns compressed/MLA attention versus MoE KV behavior across Chapters 1 and 3. Need both sections to verify whether the distinction is consistent.
The finding concerns a sidebar table versus a cost-per-request bullet. Need both quoted locations in full to verify whether the cost bases match.
The quoted inline math contains a visible LaTeX artifact: n_<TAB>ext{KV-heads}. This is a typesetting defect.
The finding concerns whether the mini-case recommendation to enable prefix caching contradicts earlier telemetry interpretation. Need the full mini-case and related sections.
The finding concerns per-rank traffic conventions for data parallelism. Need the full equation and comparison with Chapter 9 to verify whether the convention is inconsistent.
Same scope as the DeepSeek CH15-01 entry. Need the full Architect's Question and mini-case scope notes to verify the host-count logic.
Same as the DeepSeek CH16-01 entry. Need the full price-point context to determine whether per-1K-token and per-request units are being conflated.
Two 70B 4-bit GGUF models at about 35 GB each totaling about 70 GB is arithmetically plausible. Need the full footnote to verify whether the reservation/fallback claim is inconsistent.
The savings arithmetic ($23.75 - $12.59) * 730 = $8,146.80 is correct. The host-count ceiling part is truncated; need the full value to verify N = ceil(344/9).
floor(506/24.89) = 20 is correct. Need the full placement paragraph to verify whether the subsequent 13 + ... decomposition is consistent.
The percentile definition for p95 in a 100-request sample is ambiguous. Need the full ledger and percentile convention to verify whether 93rd-94th or 95th value is intended.
The finding concerns full agentic service time under 100% prefix reuse. Need the full table and W(T) derivation to verify the linear prefill assumption.
Same as the MiMo CH20-01 entry. Need the full fleet aggregate paragraph and figure caption to verify whether the planning bound is stated consistently.
The finding concerns whole-chapter consistency with earlier token/model chapters. Need the full chapter and cross-references to verify whether any prerequisite is missing or contradicted.
The finding concerns whether an ADR consequence overstates the effect on weight-read-dominated decode. Need the full ADR and decode cost model.
The finding concerns the green initialize path in Figure 2.1. Need the rendered figure to verify whether the arrow enters the wrong node.
A 70B model at FP8 has about 70 GB of resident weights, not 140 GB. 140 GB corresponds to FP16/BF16. The caption as quoted is materially wrong.
The finding concerns MoE parameter count, resident bytes, and active-compute fraction. Need the full figure and caption to verify whether ~94 GB, ~47B, and ~27% are mutually consistent.
The finding concerns visual hierarchy and whether the prominent 12 GB vs 0.6 GB boxes encode a misleading 20x reduction. Need the rendered figure and intended comparison.
The finding concerns panels B/C and the relationship between fixed prompt/causal prefix and unresolved canvas cells. Need the rendered figure to verify semantic clarity.
The finding concerns a dashed red connector pointing opposite its label/caption. Need the rendered figure to verify arrow direction.
The quoted takeaway states two mutually exclusive p99 TTFT values in one sentence. That is an internal contradiction as quoted.
If the caption formula omits the factor of 2 for K and V, it cannot reproduce the stated KV bytes per token. The quoted finding is supported.

A 64:1 query-to-KV head ratio implies a 64x reduction in KV head count relative to full MHA, not an 8x smaller footprint, unless other factors are being conflated. As quoted, the statement is inconsistent.
The finding concerns scale segment widths for NVFP4 and MXFP4. Need the rendered figure to verify whether the visual is not to scale.
The finding concerns whether the full fine-tune bar can be reconstructed from its listed components. Need the full figure note and component values.
The finding concerns Figure 8.2 prefill operating point labels. Need the rendered figure, caption, and facing-page values to verify consistency.
The quoted finding states that three figures in two chapters use two different canonical context lengths. If true, that is a cross-figure consistency defect.
1 x 4 x (31 - 1) = 120, not 121. The intended expression is likely 1 + 4 x (31 - 1). As quoted, the operator is wrong.
Ring all-reduce latency normally has two phases, so omitting a factor of 2 in the quoted equation is a likely technical error if the figure/model assumes two-phase ring traffic.

The quoted finding states that Figure 13.1 uses a tier vocabulary conflicting with the immediately preceding prose. If the figure labels differ from the section's tier list, that is a consistency defect.

A FlashAttention figure that contrasts HBM traffic should show the materialized LxL attention matrix in the naive path. If the BEFORE panel omits that object, the figure fails its core explanatory purpose.
If the y-axis says 'Prefill FLOPs / req (M)' but the caption describes the quantity as a percent of no-cache prefill, the axis label and caption are inconsistent.
The quoted title says the self-host line crosses the managed API at 6.24M req/mo, while the figure annotation says break-even is about 7.5... Those are inconsistent as quoted.
The finding concerns whether the caption's claim about quadratic attention dominance at 128K is supported by the plotted crossover. Need the full figure and calculation.

The quoted caption says the served-demand curve is 21.77 -> 22 req/s at the canonical 40 rps peak. That mixes a per-host or fractional capacity value with the fleet peak and is inconsistent as quoted.

prompt_edits: Add a mandatory canonical ledger gate: before accepting any chapter number, require the reviewer to map it to a ledger entry for request volume, tokens/request, KV GB/request, host count, cost basis, and hours/month. Flag any value that cannot be traced to one ledger row, and treat cross-chapter reuse of the same label with different bases as P1.

Add a figure arithmetic and semantic gate: for every figure, extract all numeric labels, axis ticks, percentile markers, and operator glyphs; recompute each from the caption and prose; verify percentile consistency (e.g., 1% mass at 5 s implies p99 at or above 5 s), color/legend semantics, and that drawn operators match the intended math (e.g., + vs x).

Add domain-scope and event-accounting checks: (a) table rows must be explicitly scoped inference vs training, and optimizer/gradient terms in inference tables are P1; (b) prefix-cache ledgers must distinguish initial processing from reprocessing, with total processed under 100% reuse equal to initial plus appended, not initial per call; (c) cost claims must state per-host vs total, average vs peak, and per-1K-tokens vs per-request.
